geometry_edits.rationale: Replace the cross-mass mutation with a bend to restore a single continuous dominant massing gesture.
Align the bend to the long axis to keep the bar coherent in plan.
Use a moderate angle to create continuity without producing a broken or colliding silhouette.
Increase the carved void to make the public threshold more readable and usable at the ground edge.
Anchor the void to the access side so the frontage becomes an active entry seam rather than a sealed edge.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the aggressive cross-mass mutation with a more continuous bent-bar logic so the dominant gesture becomes one readable urban bar instead of colliding wedges.
Keep the dominant gesture aligned to the long axis to preserve a compact street-building bar.
Limit the bend complexity so the silhouette remains continuous rather than fractured.
Strengthen the carved public void so the ground response to the frontage becomes legible and occupiable.
Keep the void tied to the verified access side so the entry/court reads as a true frontage response.

rationale: The candidate reads as a single mass from some angles, but the four views expose a sectional and volumetric conflict: the form collapses into a heavily slashed, book-like wedge with multiple colliding planes, and it does not consistently establish one dominant occupiable volume. The required neighborhood-living semantics are only partially present: there is some carved void logic, but the road-front access edge is not clearly translated into an active public threshold, court, or entry seam. The silhouette is closer to an arbitrary stepped/sculpted object than to a compact mixed-use bar with calm upper massing and a usable ground response. Compared with the supplied references, it borrows the idea of a void/terrace and a street-facing low mass, but the section is too aggressive and the hierarchy too fractured to support the program convincingly.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much lower, more pavilion-like and horizontally calm than the candidate; do not copy the one-story typology.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Simple rectilinear street volume with a clear corner/service element and a legible public-facing ground threshold.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is a conventional midrise infill composition, while the candidate is more aggressively faceted and sectionally unstable.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Streetwall composition with attached volumes and a setback/threshold condition that preserves urban continuity.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual principle only; the candidate does not yet achieve the coherent terrace-courtyard relationship seen here.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/courtyard massing can support neighborhood living when the void is inhabitable and the upper mass remains legible.

warnings: Visible self-collision/overlap across views suggests the mass may not compile into a stable coherent solid.
The access edge is not read as a strong public opening; the ground response feels muted relative to the program brief.
Sectional expression is overdesigned for neighborhood living and weakens the active-ground / calm-upper hierarchy.
